race.name: Elf
race.special_rule: Elves do not progress past adult.

aging_rules.rule: Apply the listed progressive ability score adjustment at each new age category.
For a character generated at an advanced age, the cumulative adjustment for the current age category may be used instead.
Ability score adjustments from aging cannot reduce an ability score below a class minimum.
Ability score adjustments from aging can never reduce an ability score below 3.

death_from_old_age.timing_rule: Each required save must be made within 1d12 months of reaching the triggering age.

triggers.trigger: Racial minimum old age plus current Constitution score.
Racial minimum ancient age plus current Constitution score.
Racial maximum listed age, and each year thereafter.

special_rules.rule: Use the character's current Constitution after age-based adjustments when determining the trigger age.
Restore life and limb does not raise characters who die from old age.

overview.rule: Optional poison use includes monster venoms, plant toxins, and magical poisons.
At Judge discretion, markets may sell monster venoms, plant toxins, and magical poisons.

condition.name: sickness
condition.effect: Move at half speed and cannot fight or perform other actions.

acquisition.rule: Naturalism proficiency identifies venomous monsters and distinguishes their poisons with a successful proficiency throw of 11+.
Extracting venom from a slain monster requires 1 day and a successful Animal Husbandry proficiency throw of 11+.
If the extraction throw is an unmodified 1, the extractor is scratched by fang or stinger and must immediately save versus Poison as if hit by the monster.

dose_rules.rule: Each monster yields one dose of venom.
One dose treats twenty missiles or one melee weapon.
Venom applied to weapons is less effective than the monster's natural venom delivery.

gathering.rule: A character with Naturalism proficiency may search for a fresh poisonous plant specimen once each week.
A successful proficiency throw against the plant's listed target value gathers enough fresh plant to extract one dose.
Dried belladonna and dried wolfsbane are commonly available in markets, but are harder to extract than fresh plants.

extraction.rule: Extracting toxin takes 1 week per plant.
Fresh plants require a successful Alchemy proficiency throw of 14+.
Dried plants require a successful Alchemy proficiency throw of 17+.
If either the gather throw or extract throw is an unmodified 1, the character is exposed and must immediately save versus Poison or suffer the toxin's effects.

dose_rules.rule: Each plant yields one dose of toxin.
If the toxin can be used on weapons, one dose treats twenty missiles or one melee weapon.
If the toxin can be used in food or drink, one dose poisons one meal or one drink.
Extracted plant toxins generally cannot be detected by smell or taste.

creation_rules.rule: Magical poisons are created using the magic research rules.
The most common magical poison is a poison potion created using the 4th level reversed divine spell poison.

dose_rules.rule: One poison potion treats twenty missiles or one melee weapon.

effects.rule: A weapon treated with magical poison kills instantly unless the victim succeeds on a saving throw versus Poison.
Magical poison is also fatal if ingested.

evaporation.rule: On the first day after application, poison does full damage.
On the second day after application, poison does half damage.
By the third day after application, the poison is gone.
Partially evaporated deadly poisons grant the victim a +2 bonus on the saving throw after the first day and a +4 bonus after the second day.
For melee weapons, each hit counts as one day of evaporation. The poison does half damage on the second hit and is gone after that.

self_injury.rule: If a character attacks with a poisoned weapon and rolls an unmodified 1, he has pricked himself.
He must immediately save versus Poison or suffer the poison's effects.

overview.rule: Optional slavery rules divide slaves into five types: slave laborers, slave soldiers, household slaves, pleasure slaves, and professional slaves.

rules.rule: Slave laborers can perform labor-related tasks.
On a domain, every 5 slave laborers count as 1 peasant family for all purposes.
If 25% or more of a domain's population is slave laborers, domain morale is reduced by 1.
If 50% or more of a domain's population is slave laborers, domain morale is reduced by 2.
If the domain is 100% slave labor, domain morale is reduced by 4.

slave_type.name: slave_soldiers
slave_type.purchase_cost: Variable by race, training, and equipment

morale_rules.rule: Slave soldiers enslaved as children have the same morale scores as normal mercenaries of their type.
Slave soldiers enslaved as adults have morale -4.
Supplemental pay, better food, access to women, and similar benefits can increase morale.

rules.rule: Better working conditions, kind treatment, gifts, or extended liberties can increase morale.

slave_type.name: pleasure_slaves
slave_type.purchase_cost: 100gp to 1000gp, with exceptional slaves able to command higher prices

rules.rule: Pleasure slaves usually have one or more ranks in Seduction, Performance (dance), or Labor (massage).
Better working conditions, kind treatment, gifts, or extended liberties can increase morale.
Professional slaves are trained experts such as scribes, tutors, or accountants.
Better working conditions, kind treatment, gifts, or extended liberties can increase morale.

definition.rule: Sinkholes of evil are corrupted places where profane powers and undead are strengthened and the divine and the living are weakened.
Sinkholes may be shadowed, blighted, or forsaken.

entry.undead_in_sinkhole: +2 attack throws, saving throws, damage rolls, and AC
entry.animating_undead: +2 hit points per Hit Die and double normal Hit Dice created

source.name: chaotic_altar
source.rule: A chaotic altar creates a shadowed sinkhole immediately when erected.
Area equals 100 square feet per 100gp spent on the altar.
At Judge discretion, the altar's gp value may be satisfied by special components or blood sacrifices instead of standard treasure.

source.name: place_of_death
source.rule: Each year, a place of death has a percentage chance to become shadowed equal to the number of dead interred divided by the site's square footage, rounded up.
When the sinkhole develops, its size is 100 square feet per 20 dead interred.
A sinkhole does not develop if the dead are cremated by a Lawful divine spellcaster.
A sinkhole does not develop if one or more shrines to Lawful powers are erected on the site with a total value of at least 5gp per dead interred.

effects.rule: Corpses in a shadowed sinkhole have a 10% chance to return as undead in 1d12 months unless burned.
Chaotic spellcasters casting reversed divine spells or necromantic spells in a shadowed sinkhole resolve those spells as if 2 class levels higher.
Necromancy research in a shadowed sinkhole gains a +1 bonus to magic research throws.
A shadowed sinkhole may be used for blood sacrifice.

creation.rule: A blighted sinkhole forms where a chaotic altar stands on a shadowed place of death.
The blighted area extends only where the altar's shadowing and the place of death's shadowing overlap.
Areas affected by only one source remain merely shadowed.

effects.rule: Corpses in a blighted sinkhole have a 20% chance to return as undead in 1d4 days unless burned.
Chaotic spellcasters casting reversed divine spells or necromantic spells in a blighted sinkhole resolve those spells as if 2 class levels higher.
Lawful divine spellcasters turn undead as if 4 class levels lower.
Necromancy research in a blighted sinkhole gains a +2 bonus to magic research throws.
A blighted sinkhole may be used for blood sacrifice.

creation.rule: A blighted area may become forsaken through rare planar conjunctions or terrible ritual magic.
Forsaken sinkholes are very rare and occur at Judge discretion.

effects.rule: Corpses in a forsaken sinkhole have an 80% chance to return as undead in 1d4 rounds unless burned.
Chaotic spellcasters casting reversed divine spells or necromantic spells in a forsaken sinkhole resolve those spells as if 2 class levels higher.
Lawful divine spellcasters cast spells as if 2 class levels lower for spell effects.
Lawful divine spellcasters may not turn undead in a forsaken sinkhole.
Undead in a forsaken sinkhole gain +2 to attack throws, saving throws, damage rolls, and AC.
Necromancy research in a forsaken sinkhole gains a +3 bonus to magic research throws.
Undead created in a forsaken sinkhole gain a permanent +2 hit points per Hit Die.
Animate dead cast in a forsaken sinkhole creates twice the normal number of Hit Dice of undead.
A forsaken sinkhole may be used for blood sacrifice.

temporary_cleansing.rule: A bless spell temporarily reduces the sinkhole's severity within a 100 foot diameter area for the spell's duration.
While affected by bless, a shadowed area becomes cleansed, a blighted area becomes shadowed, and a forsaken area becomes blighted.
A vial of holy water sprinkled on a 10 foot diameter area has the same temporary effect as bless.

permanent_cleansing.rule: To permanently cleanse a sinkhole, remove its source of corruption.
If the source is a chaotic altar, destroy it either with dispel evil or by physically smashing it and then applying holy water or bless to the remains.
Destroying the altar removes the sinkhole created by that altar.
If the source is a place of death, dispel evil instantly cleanses the sinkhole, but it will eventually return unless the source is permanently addressed.
To permanently cleanse a place of death, a Lawful divine spellcaster must cremate the dead interred there or erect a shrine to the Lawful powers of sufficient value.
Cleansing a blighted sinkhole requires addressing both the chaotic altar and the place of death separately.
A forsaken sinkhole can only be permanently cleansed by ritual magic.
The ritual to cleanse a forsaken sinkhole is usually forgotten between occurrences and must normally be researched anew by Lawful forces.

core_rules.rule: An adventurer transformed into an intelligent monster may continue to be played with Judge permission.

The Judge determines the transformed character's alignment based on the transformation context. Transformed characters generally adopt the alignment of the new form unless exceptionally strong-willed or purposeful.
The transformed character gains the movement modes, speeds, natural armor, natural attacks, extraordinary abilities, and other abilities of the new form.
If the monster's Hit Dice are lower than the character's former class level, raise the monster's Hit Dice to the former class level.
A transformed character may gain additional Hit Dice through adventuring.

advancement.rule: For a 1 HD monster to advance to 2 HD, required XP equals 3000 plus 500 per special ability marker (*).
The XP required doubles with each additional Hit Die.
XP values greater than 20000 are rounded to the nearest 1000.

class_abilities.rule: In most cases, the transformed character loses all class abilities.
At Judge discretion, transformed spellcasters may retain spellcasting.
Retained divine spellcasting counts as one special ability marker (*).
Retained arcane spellcasting counts as two special ability markers (**).
As the transformed character gains Hit Dice, retained spellcasting advances using the prior class's spellcasting progression, subject to that class's maximum level.

tier.name: adventurer
tier.campaign_scope: Action and exploration oriented campaigns with experienced players.

tier.name: conqueror
tier.campaign_scope: Campaigns focused on establishing and expanding domains.

tier.name: king
tier.campaign_scope: Campaigns focused on realm management and warfare.

ability_score_generation.rule: Roll 3d6 in order five times and choose one full set of rolls as the character's ability scores.
Conquerors may reroll one ability score from the chosen set and must use the new roll.
Kings may reroll two ability scores from the chosen set and must use the new rolls.

hit_points.rule: Advanced characters receive maximum hit points at 1st level.
Remaining Hit Dice are rolled normally.

notes.note: Places elven spellswords at 4th level, thieves at 6th level, and most other classes at 5th level.
Places elven spellswords at 8th level, clerics and thieves at 10th level, and most other classes at 9th level.
Most racial classes are at or near maximum level.
Mages are 11th level, clerics and thieves are 13th level, and most other classes are 12th level.

class_and_level.rule: Advanced characters may choose any class they qualify for.
Level is determined by the class's progression table and the campaign's fixed starting experience point total.

proficiencies.rule: All advanced characters begin knowing any proficiencies they qualify for based on class, level, and Intelligence score.

spell_repertoire.rule: Mages, elven nightblades, and elven spellswords begin with the maximum number of spells in their repertoire.
Adventurers determine all repertoire spells randomly.
Conquerors choose half their repertoire spells and determine the rest randomly.
Kings choose all spells in their repertoire.

permitted_uses.use: Purchase equipment such as weapons, armor, ships, and mounts.
Establish libraries, workshops, laboratories, or mortuaries.
Purchase precious materials or special components.
Build castles, hideouts, sanctums, or other strongholds.
Trade wealth for rolls for magic items.

starting_wealth.remainder_rule: Unspent starting wealth may be converted into coin, gems, or jewels.

trade_limits.rule: Each listed trade may be made once by adventurers and conquerors.
Kings may make each listed trade twice, funds permitting.

trade.result: 15% chance of two random magic items.
25% chance of one weapon or armor, 25% chance of one potion, and 10% chance of one miscellaneous magic item.
50% chance of four randomly determined magic items, one random potion, and one random scroll.
1d4 random potions, 1d4 random scrolls, and 50% chance of six randomly determined magic items.
2d4 random potions, 2d4 random scrolls, and 75% chance each for 1d3 swords, 1d3 armor, 1d3 miscellaneous weapons, 1d3 wands/staffs/rods, 1d3 rings, and 1d3 miscellaneous magic items.

special_rules.rule: The Judge may randomly determine or choose the actual magic items.
Characters capable of magic research may substitute formulas for actual magic items at a 2:1 ratio.
Example conversion: 1d4 random potions may be replaced with 2d4 potion formulas.

henchmen.rule: An advanced character may begin with henchmen up to the limit allowed by Charisma.
A henchman may be any class or level.
The advanced character must spend gp equal to the henchman's experience points.
The advanced character must provide the henchman's equipment and magic items.

specialists_and_mercenaries.rule: An advanced character may also begin with specialists and mercenaries.
For each specialist or mercenary, the advanced character must spend gp equal to six months of wages.
This cost represents past retainer expenses.

conqueror_tier.rule: Conqueror-tier characters of 9th level or higher who use starting wealth to build a stronghold begin play with a domain.
Create the domain as if the stronghold has just been completed, including rolling starting land value, peasant families, and followers.
If the character builds a hideout, the syndicate has the standard followers: 2d6 1st level characters of the boss's class, plus 1d6 more per level beyond 9th.
If the character builds a sanctum, the sanctum has the standard followers: 1d6 apprentices and 2d6 normal men.
Dungeons built by conqueror-tier characters begin empty.

king_tier.rule: King-tier characters who use starting wealth to build a stronghold begin play with a realm.
The realm includes a personal domain and several vassal realms.
The personal domain begins with the maximum number of families allowed by the stronghold's size.
The number of vassal realms equals the character's number of henchmen.
Each vassal realm is normally equivalent to a duchy, though the Judge may alter the scope.
King-tier thieves, assassins, and elven nightblades who build a hideout begin with a syndicate of maximum size for the location and hideout.
If such a character has thief, assassin, or nightblade henchmen of 9th level or higher, those henchmen may build hideouts and establish a criminal guild.
Syndicates within that criminal guild have 2d6 members each.
King-tier mages who build a sanctum begin with 6 third-level mage apprentices and 12 normal men.
If a king-tier mage builds a dungeon, it should begin populated until full.

location_rule.rule: The Judge may determine the starting location of strongholds, domains, and realms, or allow the characters to choose locations on the regional map.
